status_summary: Interior reports that CEQ rescinded its government-wide NEPA regulations by an interim final rule (effective 2025-04-11) and finalized the rescission on 2026-01-08. Interior published an interim final rule on 2025-07-03 and a final rule on 2026-02-24 that removes most of its NEPA procedures from 43 CFR part 46 and moves them to a non-codified handbook, relying on the Supreme Court's 2025 Seven County decision. On 2026-08-20 Interior finalized two BLM categorical exclusions for timber salvage and thinning. The design differs from the Mandate, which asked to reinstate the 2020 CEQ rules and secretarial orders, and no congressional change to NEPA judicial review was found.

timeline.event: CEQ publishes an interim final rule (90 FR 10610) removing its NEPA implementing regulations from the Code of Federal Regulations and requesting comment; it takes effect 2025-04-11 (next entry).
CEQ's interim final rule removing its NEPA implementing regulations takes effect (effective date stated in the rule published 2025-02-25).
Interior publishes an interim final rule, National Environmental Policy Act Implementing Regulations, with a 30-day comment period (description from Interior's 2026 final rule).
Center for Biological Diversity and Sierra Club sue in the Northern District of California to vacate Interior's July 2025 NEPA interim final rule (month only; first of month used).

CEQ publishes a final rule (91 FR 618, effective the same day) removing its NEPA implementing regulations from the Code of Federal Regulations; it adopts the February 2025 interim final rule as final without changes.

Interior publishes its final NEPA rule, effective the same day: most procedures leave 43 CFR part 46 for a handbook, while emergency response, categorical exclusions, applicant-prepared documents and lead and cooperating agency provisions stay in regulation.
Interior publishes notices of two finalized NEPA categorical exclusions, timber salvage harvest and forest and woodland density management, for BLM projects up to 5,000 acres (announced 2026-08-20).
Interior establishes, effective on publication, a categorical exclusion in its NEPA Handbook for BLM wintertime oil and gas exploration in the National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska (91 FR 64673).
